summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35.46% YoY to ₹387 crores and PAT rose 55.97% to ₹24.07 crores, while the new CCL line remains pre-revenue and guidance is under revision.
summary.overview: Ratnaveer reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹387 crores (+35.46% YoY), EBITDA of ₹42.13 crores (+38.85%) and PAT of ₹24.07 crores (+55.97%), which management called the highest in company history. Gross margin dipped to 9.44% in Q2 from 10.33% in Q1, which management attributed to expenses for new products being booked before CCL sales begin. The company is building its first Copper Clad Laminate (CCL) line under the ECMS scheme, targeting trial runs from December 20, 2026 and staged ramp-up across five lines by April 2028. Management said earlier CCL guidance (₹750 crores from five lines, 20% EBITDA, 13% PAT) will be revised soon because CCL prices have risen sharply, but did not give new numbers.

financial_highlights.value: 10.82% (as stated by management); analyst cited 9.4%, management gave gross margin of 9.44%

financial_highlights.metric: Return on equity / Return on capital employed

segments.name: Base business (stainless steel fasteners, clips, washers, tubes and pipes, finishing line, sheet metal)
segments.commentary: Revenue was ₹1,080 crores last year and management expects ₹1,315 crores this year, with a target of ₹1,800 crores by FY28. Finishing line is running near capacity; ₹58 crores of capex this year supports Phase 2 expansion.

segments.name: CCL (Copper Clad Laminate, new line)
segments.commentary: Not yet booking revenue; first line of 15 lakh sheets is targeted to start trial run in December 2026. Planned investment is ₹338 crores over two to three years plus ₹86 crores for a captive solar plant.

guidance_outlook: Earlier CCL guidance (₹750 crores from five lines, 20% EBITDA, 13% PAT) is being kept for now; management said a revised guidance will be announced very soon, with no figures given.
FY28 consolidated targets quoted on old guidance: ₹2,500 crores top line, 14% EBITDA and 11% PAT; management also referred to a 10% consolidated PAT guidance for FY28 and a 13% PAT aspiration.
Full-year FY27 PAT margin expected at around 6.25%; effective tax rate expected near last year's ~15%.
Target of 7-8% share of the Indian CCL market in five years (about 2% today with five lines).
Management said a single CCL line could generate ₹500 crores revenue at current prices, versus ₹150 crores per line in earlier guidance.
capex_capacity: CCL project about 75% complete; civil work almost done. Machinery shipped and expected in India by 15-20 November 2026, with 45-50 days for erection and commissioning.
Trial run targeted 15-20 December 2026 to 20 January 2027, with product run from December 20. Utilisation ramp: 30% in February 2027, 60% by March, 85% by April 2027 (first line).
Line roadmap: line 2 starts June 2027, line 3 September 2027, lines 4 and 5 January and April 2028; orders for lines 2-3 to be placed in December-January.
Chinese team of 22 engineers plus one Chief Technical Officer (30 years' experience) to install machines; one person to stay for two years.
Products: CCL with Tg 140-180, copper thickness 15-35 microns, board thickness 0.8-3.2 mm; FR4 and prepreg, single and double-sided, multi-layer capable.
Phase 2 capex for fasteners, tubes and pipes, sheet metal and clips is ongoing.
demand_pricing: CCL prices have risen by more than 300% over the past year per management, while raw material costs rose 40-50% at most; no Indian CCL producers exist today, and Chinese, Taiwan and Korean suppliers have limited export capacity.

Initial bookings: pricing at par with Chinese imports or 0.5-1% below. Customers get wait-time, logistics, FX and faster delivery benefits. Government offers a 2% incentive to CCL buyers, per management.
Orders received from two companies (Indian PCB makers); long-term contract talks with seven companies. Management expects order confirmations to be announced in about two to three weeks.
Marketing: 57 visits to PCB customers; enquiries from Japan, the US and Europe.
Management expects no competition or anti-dumping duty in the near term; sees the market growing at 50-70% CAGR. Wipro is named as another CCL entrant; Syrma SGS reportedly postponing its CCL plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin expected to expand from about 10% to 13%, and what are the volume numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a shift from volume to value and higher CCL margins. Volume figures were not given; revenue was cited instead: ₹1,080 crores last year and ₹1,315 crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CCL trial timeline and utilisation ramp, and is the 85% target for the first two lines?
qa_highlights.answer: The first line starts trial run 15-20 December; utilisation targets are 30% in February, 60% in March and 85% in April 2027. Line 2 starts June 2027, and all five lines are expected to be installed by April 2028.

qa_highlights.question: How do margins respond to CCL price changes, and what grades are targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CCL prices rose 300%+ on shortage, with raw material up only 40-50%, so PCB makers should pass the increase on. The plant covers Tg 140-180 for PCB, automotive, EV, drone, satellite and aerospace uses.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any anti-dumping duty risk on CCL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no duty is in discussion because there is no domestic producer, so no injury to local industry can exist.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the employee cost low, and when will customer ramp-up happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of employee cost is capitalised into projects and part is booked as job-work charges, and it is well controlled. Order confirmations and long-term contracts are to be announced in the next couple of weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and cash flow outlook, and are there any commissioning risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rights issue gives enough liquidity for working capital, term loans cover most of the five lines, and a 50% cash subsidy will return part of capex. Operating cash flow is negative only because of capex; no delay is seen, though two to three weeks of teething issues are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall in Q2, and what is the FY27 PAT margin and tax rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin fell to 9.44% from 10.33% in Q1 because costs for new products were booked before CCL sales. FY27 PAT margin is expected at about 6.25%, with an effective tax rate near last year's ~15%.

risks_watch: CCL commissioning timeline: machines due mid-November, 45-50 days to install, trial run from 15-20 December; any slip pushes revenue beyond FY27.
Revised CCL guidance is promised 'very soon' but no figures were given; the ₹500 crore per-line claim is management's own and unaudited.
Operating cash flow is negative and the new segments have raised inventory and receivables; cash flow improvement depends on capex stabilising.
Gross margin dipped to 9.44% in Q2; new product costs are being expensed before CCL revenue starts.
Order book: no firm CCL order values disclosed; confirmations promised within two to three weeks.
Customer, Chinese-supplier and engineering dependence; a 22-plus-1 person Chinese team is needed for installation.
summary.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional on CCL, with repeated forward-looking claims (₹500 crores per line, 300% price rise, 85% utilisation by April 2027). On specifics like new guidance figures, order names, the margin guidance and EBITDA margin drivers, management was evasive and deferred answers to future announcements.
key_quotes: There is a huge margin gap that can open up, and the bottom line can improve drastically.
Very soon we will be present with the new guidance and the revised numbers.
The company has already been receiving orders from two companies.
Once this CapEx stabilises and all the capacities are fully operational, the cash flow will definitely turn positive.

adds.what: First CCL line, 15 lakh sheets (Ratnaveer Copper Clad Laminate line under ECMS)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 core revenue to ₹1,315 cr (about +22% on ₹1,080 cr, so roughly 21-22%) and FY28 core target ₹1,800 cr, backed by capacity expansion and two CCL orders plus seven in talks, but CCL line 1 is not yet live (trial Dec 2026), CCL guidance is being withdrawn for revision with no new numbers, and no concrete order values were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided margin to expand from about 10% to 13% on a shift to CCL value and higher CCL margins, though Q2 gross margin fell to 9.44% from 10.33% in Q1 as new-product costs are booked before CCL sales and FY27 PAT margin is guided at about 6.25%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: CCL line 1 (15 lakh sheets, ₹338 cr capex) is about 75% complete with machines due mid-November and trial run from 15-20 December 2026, then line 2 in June 2027, line 3 in September 2027 and lines 4-5 by April 2028.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Base business revenue guided to ₹1,315 cr this year vs ₹1,080 cr last year (about +21-22%), with CCL utilisation targeted at 30% in February, 60% in March and 85% in April 2027 on the first line, though no volume figures were given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Orders for CCL lines 2-3 are to be placed in December-January, Phase 2 capex for fasteners, tubes, sheet metal and clips is ongoing with ₹58 cr this year, and a ₹86 cr captive solar plant is planned alongside the ₹338 cr CCL investment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says revised CCL guidance will be announced 'very soon' because CCL prices rose over 300% and it claims ₹500 cr revenue per line vs ₹150 cr in earlier guidance, but no new figures were given and the claim is unaudited.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Any slip in the 45-50 day install after mid-November machine arrival would push the 15-20 December trial run and revenue beyond FY27, and Q2 gross margin already dipped to 9.44%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First CCL product (Tg 140-180, 15-35 micron copper, 0.8-3.2 mm board) has a product run from 20 December 2026, with two Indian PCB makers already ordering and seven in long-term contract talks.

rows.label: CCL order confirmations
rows.why: Orders from two Indian PCB makers received and long-term talks with seven companies, with confirmations promised in about two to three weeks, though no order values were disclosed.

rows.label: CCL pricing at par to 0.5-1% below Chinese imports
rows.why: Initial bookings priced at par with Chinese imports or 0.5-1% below, with CCL prices up over 300% in a year and raw material up only 40-50%, and no Indian CCL producers exist today.

rows.label: Rights issue and 50% cash subsidy support liquidity
rows.why: Management says the rights issue funds working capital, term loans cover most of the five lines, and a 50% cash subsidy returns part of capex, though operating cash flow is negative due to capex.

tone.note: Management was highly confident on CCL pricing, the 85% utilisation target and the ₹500 cr per-line claim, but evasive on revised guidance figures, order values and the margin bridge. Analysts pushed on margin expansion, volume numbers, cash flow and commissioning risk.
